metadata.name: Social Democracy
metadata.description: Reformist social democracy combining competitive democracy, a mixed economy, labour rights and inclusive social provision.
metadata.period: Post-war European reformism; 1989 principles with 2026 policy context
metadata.scope: Reformist parliamentary social democracy, combining a mixed economy, universal social provision and labour rights. The Socialist International declaration includes democratic-socialist aspirations; this profile selects its explicit mixed-economy formulation rather than assuming total social ownership. This is a sourced interpretation of the specified tradition, not an adherent questionnaire. Unresolved evidence or an unrepresented institutional premise is recorded as unknown, never as numerical neutrality. Historical sources are not treated as answers to modern technologies by analogy. Government acts are contextual evidence only, not a substitute for the scoped doctrine.
metadata.phrase: A democratic society combining a regulated market economy with social insurance, labour rights and redistribution.

Repeated subsidy neither automatically warrants privatisation nor guarantees retention; the actual policy is conditional on wider public benefit.
